body:
Shares of Pricol Ltd plunged as much as 20% in opening deals on Monday, November 16, after the firm announced that its promoters will sell their entire 38.51% stake in the company’s automotive electronics business to global private equity firm Warburg Pincus after it is demerged into a separate entity.

Demat Account within minutes!

A regulatory filing said on Friday that Warburg Pincus will subsequently make an open offer to acquire an additional 26% stake in the new entity from public shareholders.

Pricol and Warburg Pincus jointly announced that they have signed definitive agreements for the proposed acquisition, which will take place after the demerger of Pricol’s Driver Information and Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business into Pricol Autotech and its subsequent listing on the NSE and BSE.

According to media reports, the sharp decline in Pricol shares may be linked to investor concerns over the valuation of the demerged business.

The proposed transaction values Pricol Autotech at around ₹4,300 crore, which some market participants reportedly consider less attractive than expected.

The proposed acquisition is subject to the demerger becoming effective and requisite regulatory and other approvals.

Pricol’s board had approved a scheme of arrangement for the demerger on June 27, 2026. Under the scheme, eligible shareholders of Pricol Ltd are expected to receive one equity share of Pricol Autotech for every equity share held in the parent company.

Pricol Autotech will house the DICVS business, which provides driver information systems and automotive electronics, including instrument clusters, telematics, sensors and e-cockpit solutions. It caters to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across the two-wheeler, three-wheeler, passenger vehicle, commercial vehicle and off-highway segments.

The DICVS business reported revenue of approximately ₹2,400 crore in FY26, accounting for around 60% of Pricol’s consolidated revenue.

Following the scheme becoming effective, Warburg Pincus will launch a mandatory open offer to acquire up to an additional 26% of Pricol Autotech’s share capital from public shareholders, in accordance with applicable SEBI regulations.

Upon completion of the transaction, Warburg Pincus will become the largest shareholder in the demerged entity.

The scheme and proposed transaction are subject to various approvals and conditions, including those from shareholders, creditors, stock exchanges, SEBI, the National Company Law Tribunal and the Competition Commission of India, as applicable.

Following the demerger, Pricol Ltd will continue to operate its Actuation, Control and Fluid Management Systems (ACFMS) business, while its Polymer business will operate through its wholly owned subsidiary, Pricol Precision Products Pvt Ltd.

Both businesses will remain under the ownership and management of the existing promoter group, the Mohan family, with no change in their shareholding, the filing said.

What the Pricol Chairman said

Pricol Chairman and Managing Director Vikram Mohan said the proposed demerger would give Pricol Autotech the focus and independence to realise its full potential. He said Warburg Pincus, with its global presence, resources, connections and automotive sector expertise, was the right partner to take the business forward.

Warburg Pincus' top officials’ statement

Anish Saraf, Managing Director at Warburg Pincus, said the firm looked forward to partnering with Pricol Autotech’s management and employees to support the company’s long-term ambitions and expand its presence in India and internationally.

Swapnil Sinha, another Managing Director at Warburg Pincus, said the automotive components sector had long been an area of focus for the firm in India. He said the growing sophistication of vehicle technology presented opportunities in automotive electronics.

The firm aims to support Pricol Autotech’s growth through investments in technology and talent, expansion of capabilities and customer relationships, and strategic acquisitions, he added.

The proposed transaction is expected to build on Pricol Autotech’s existing capabilities in instrument clusters, connected vehicle technologies and e-cockpit solutions, to develop a broader automotive electronics business.

Emkay Global is positive on the stock. The investment firm said the proposed demerger of the company's Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business will create two focused businesses. Warburg Pincus is set to acquire the promoters' 38.5% stake in the demerged entity for around ₹1,700 crore, valuing the business at approximately ₹4,300 crore.

Emkay believes Warburg Pincus's entry could accelerate the automotive electronics business's expansion, technology partnerships and global growth. Existing Pricol shareholders are expected to receive shares of Pricol Autotech in a 1:1 ratio following the demerger.

The investment firm expects Pricol to deliver a revenue CAGR of 21%, EBITDA CAGR of 24% and EPS CAGR of 26% between FY26 and FY29.
